title: AFS licensing: Organisational competence
subject: This guide describes ASIC's approach to assessing compliance with the organisational competence obligation for Australian financial services (AFS) licensees and applicants. It covers what ASIC looks for when evaluating whether a licensee has the knowledge and skills to provide financial services competently.
background: The guide is issued under the Corporations Act 2001 (Cth) and explains ASIC's interpretation of the organisational competence obligation in s912A(1). It is intended for AFS licensees and AFS licence applicants to help them understand how to meet this general obligation.
ruling: ASIC expects AFS licensees to have sufficient knowledge and skills among their responsible managers and key personnel to provide financial services competently, honestly and fairly. The guide outlines that ASIC will assess the nature, scale and complexity of the licensee's business when determining organisational competence. ASIC states that responsible managers must have appropriate qualifications and experience relevant to the financial services provided. The guide also provides that licensees must maintain organisational competence on an ongoing basis, not just at the time of licensing. ASIC may take compliance measures if a licensee fails to meet this obligation, including suspending or cancelling the licence.
